To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a patient having PH with anti-Dsg1 autoantibodies was successfully treated with oral administration of dapsone and prednisolone, and that the serum anti-Dsg1 antibody titer in this case was not correlated with the disease activity.

a 27-year-old Japanese woman with a 1-year background of recurrent, pruritic, vesicular and erosive lesions on the trunk and limbs was diagnosed as PH by histopathological findings and immunofluorescence studies, but not by ELISA and immunohistochemistry for Dsgs.

a patient with sporadic PH was diagnosed as PH based on the presence of circulating autoantibody to Dsg1, but that the in vivo-bound autoantibody was not detected by immunoblotting using the patient serum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a rare case of PH, which showed a positive result in the in vivo-bound IgG ELISA, but a negative result in the circulating IgG ELISA.
the first case of PH showing positive immunofluorescence of IgG in the epidermal inter-cellular spaces.
the clinical and immunological characteristics of an unusual case of PH with a unique immunoreactivity of autoantibodies to the in vivo bound antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our patient had an unusual form of PH, in which anti-Dsg antibodies were not detectable in either ELISA or immunoblotting assays.
the patient presented here is a case of PH, and the anti-Dsg1 antibody detected by the Dsg1-specific ELISA was not the major pathogenic factor in this patient.
our patient had PH, which was not associated with Dsg antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patient with PH may be a good model to investigate the immunopathogenic mechanism of this rare disease.
PH should not be considered a simple clinical entity but rather a complex and heterogeneous disorder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PH should be considered in the differential diagnosis of a patient presenting with a vesicular and bullous eruption, particularly when accompanied with oral mucosal involvement.
the clinical and immunological heterogeneity in PH should be recognized, as it is a unique disease entity that is different from other well-defined immuno-bullae.
a careful histological evaluation is essential to make the correct diagnosis of PH.
